name: deadends-dev

tools.name: lookup_error
tools.description: Match an error message against deadends.dev's database of known errors. Returns dead ends (what NOT to try), workarounds (what works), and error chains (what comes next). Use this BEFORE attempting to fix any error to avoid wasting time on approaches that are known to fail. Covers 51 domains including python, node, docker, git, cuda, typescript, rust, go, kubernetes, terraform, aws, react, java, database, pytorch, tensorflow, and 34 more. Use list_error_domains to see all.

error_message.description: The full error message to look up

format.description: Response format: 'markdown' (default, human-readable) or 'json' (structured, for programmatic use by AI agents)

tools.name: get_error_detail
tools.description: Get full details for a specific error by its ID (e.g., 'python/modulenotfounderror/py311-linux'). Includes all dead ends, workarounds, error chain info, and source evidence.

tools.name: list_error_domains
tools.description: List all error domains and counts in the deadends.dev database. Covers 51 domains including programming languages, frameworks, infrastructure, ML/AI, culture, safety, medical, legal, and more.

sort_by.description: Sort domains by: 'count' (default, most errors first) or 'name' (alphabetical)

tools.name: search_errors
tools.description: Search errors by keyword across all domains. Unlike lookup_error (which uses regex matching), this does fuzzy keyword search. Use when you have a vague description like 'memory issues' or 'permission denied' rather than an exact error message.

domain.description: Optional: filter to a specific domain (e.g., 'python', 'docker')

tools.name: list_errors_by_domain
tools.description: List all errors in a specific domain with their fix rates. Use this to understand coverage for a domain before relying on it.

domain.description: The domain to list errors for (e.g., 'python', 'kubernetes')

tools.name: batch_lookup
tools.description: Look up multiple error messages at once. Returns the best match for each error. Use when debugging a chain of errors or analyzing a log with multiple failures.

error_messages.description: List of error messages to look up (max 10)

tools.name: get_domain_stats
tools.description: Get detailed statistics for a domain: error counts, average fix rate, resolvability breakdown, top categories, and confidence levels. Use this to assess how trustworthy deadends.dev data is for a domain.

domain.description: The domain to get stats for

tools.name: list_errors_by_country
tools.description: List all country-scoped dead ends for a given country (ISO alpha-2 code, e.g. 'kr', 'jp', 'us', 'de'). Returns visa, banking, legal, cultural, medical, food-safety, emergency, and safety dead ends specific to that jurisdiction. Use this when an AI agent needs jurisdiction-specific knowledge that global LLM training data won't reliably cover.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, lowercase (e.g. 'kr' for Korea, 'jp' for Japan)

tools.name: get_country_summary
tools.description: Get a country-level summary: total entries, domain breakdown, average fix rate, and most-recent updates for the country. Use this to assess coverage for a country before relying on deadends.dev for trip / business / legal planning advice.

tools.name: get_error_chain
tools.description: Traverse the error transition graph for a specific error. Shows what errors typically follow this one (leads_to), what errors usually precede it (preceded_by), and what errors are frequently confused with it. Use this to diagnose cascading failures and predict what comes next.

error_id.description: The error ID (domain/slug/env) to get the transition graph for

tools.name: report_outcome
tools.description: Report whether a workaround from deadends.dev worked or failed. This feedback improves fix_success_rate and confidence for future users. Call this AFTER applying a workaround to help improve the database. Accepts the error ID, the workaround action you tried, and whether it succeeded.

workaround_action.description: The workaround action string you tried (from the workarounds list)

success.description: Whether the workaround resolved the error

environment.description: Optional: your environment info (runtime, os, version, etc.)

instructions: Use lookup_error BEFORE attempting to fix any error to avoid wasting time on known dead ends. Use search_errors for vague descriptions, get_error_detail for full info by ID, and get_error_chain to predict cascading failures.
